Sean / Laura,

Thanks for the quick intro yesterday. Shipyard.ai is moving into the final evaluation for our internal LLM serving partner and we need a short evidence packet to accompany the procurement RFP (SHIP-9072). The items we require for the security/compliance section are:

- SAST/DAST program overview (tools, cadence, ownership)
- Recent pen test executive summary (last 12 months) + high-level remediation status

Team — attaching the items Sean outlined. Below is the summary text I'll include in the packet (keeps answers short for procurement):

SAST / DAST program- Tools used: Semgrep (SAST) for infra and application rules, Bandit/Custom linters for python infra, Burp Suite + OWASP ZAP (DAST) for runtime app scans.
- Cadence: SAST on every PR (pre-merge), weekly aggregate SAST reports. DAST run nightly against our staging cluster and full DAST + authentication-flows monthly.
- Ownership: AppSec triage team (So. Lee) owns tuning + false positive management; Engineering teams own fix backlog tracked in Jira (SEC tags).

Pen Test (last 12 months)- Engagement: Third-party pen test completed 2026-08 by RedCloak Security.
- Executive summary: One high-risk finding (privilege escalation in internal admin endpoint) reported; mitigated within 72 hours and validated by follow-up testing. Three medium findings (improper input sanitation, minor auth token handling) resolved within the 30-day remediation SLA.
- Evidence: pentest-summary-redwood-2026-08.pdf (executive summary + remediation timeline).

Patch SLAs and Escalation- Critical (CVSS >= 9.0 or exploit in the wild): 48 hours to patch/mitigate, 24-hour mitigation workaround where applicable, and incident notification within 2 hours to customer security contacts.
- High/Important (CVSS 7.0–8.9): 7 calendar days to patch or implement compensating control.
- Normal/Low: scheduled per monthly maintenance windows (typical 30–90 days depending on risk).
- Escalation flow: Engineer -> On-call Security -> Security Lead -> VP Ops; we include customers on status updates for critical events.

SBOM and transitive dependencies- Exported as CSV and generated from our build pipeline (CycloneDX compatible). The SBOM includes direct and transitive dependencies at build-time for the specific runtime container images referenced in the RFP. Note: runtime SBOM is generated per image tag; we provide the exact tag used in production. File: redwood_sbom-2026-09-21.csv

SOC 2 and attestations- We host SOC 2 Type II reports under NDA. For procurement purposes we can provide a SOC 2 pointer and the compliance contact; if Shipyard requires an on-file PDF we can arrange a DocuSign NDA and provide the report.

Attachments included in Drive: pentest-summary-redwood-2026-08.pdf, redwood_sbom-2026-09-21.csv, patch-sla-table.csv

If Shipyard wants raw SAST scan exports or full DAST logs for ingestion into a vulnerability management tool, we can provide them under an encrypted transfer; note that raw exports include internal identifiers and should be shared under an NDA.

—Soojin Lee
Staff AppSec Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai

Thanks — this is great context. Two quick clarifications so we can pass to our security committee:

1) For the SBOM: can you confirm the CSV includes transitive dependencies (yes/no) and the SBOM generation date / image tag? We need the SBOM to match the build used in the benchmark tests in the RFP.
2) For Patch SLAs: when you say "incident notification within 2 hours" for critical — does that include a targeted remediation ETA in that initial communication? Our CISO prefers a T minus ETA in first notice.

Also, do you have a named SOC 2 contact we can email to coordinate access/NDA? If you can share the Drive link and an expected time you will upload the artifacts, procurement can cross-check against the RFP checklist.

—Aisha

Hi Aisha — thanks for the follow-ups. We uploaded the packet to a read-only Drive folder and included short README notes for each artifact: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c4D_example (Drive link is view-only unless you request access).

Answers inline:
1) SBOM: Yes — redwood_sbom-2026-09-21.csv includes direct and transitive dependencies for the specific container image tag: redwood-runtime:v2026-08-31-rc2. The CSV includes columns: package_name, version, scope (direct/transitive), license, sha256.

2) Patch SLA initial notification: for Critical issues we send an initial notification within 2 hours that always includes an initial remediation ETA estimate (T+X hours) and the assigned remediation owner. The initial ETA is conservative and updated as we triage; for the recent pen-test critical finding the initial ETA was T+24 hours and the final mitigation was completed in 72 hours with follow-up validation (see pentest-summary-redwood-2026-08.pdf).

SOC 2 contact: Laura Bennett (laura_bennett@redwood.ai) manages compliance access. If you send an NDA link or DocuSign, Laura will coordinate delivery of the SOC 2 package.

Attached (in Drive): pentest-summary-redwood-2026-08.pdf, redwood_sbom-2026-09-21.csv, patch-sla-table.csv
